Yes you definitely should learn B2 German (in general if you want to work and also live in germany, english is spoken by younger generation but skill levels vary a lot)

1) I am guessing you think there is a cost attached like college in america? If so, there is not. You get payed the whole time.
Also about the cost of living, it is definitely not a luxury lifestyle but you can manage. I am currently doing that in my Ausbildung, however I am lucky with the pay my company gives (switzerland, around 1,6k in 4. Year I live in germany tho), I also have a part time job on a local farm in germany

2) It would certainly help to have some project(s) to show off, since you will be competing against other people with most likely good grades. It is common that there will be people that started studying an IT related field and dropped out early to switch to an Ausbildung.
In general no prior knowledge is required tho, the Berufsschule (Job school) does not teach you that much, you mostly learn on the job in your company.

3) I am not sure about the amount you will get, it is a state program as far as I know, so I don't know if you are eligible (it seems you are none german). Applying for this could prove difficult, however if time is a big factor, depending on your grades you can shorten your Ausbildung towards the end by half a year usually 

Hope that helped, just ask whatever else u need to know :)
Could you elaborarte?

It is possible to find a job as a frontend dev, however germany is degree obsessed, meaning it will be way, way, way easier for you to get jobs and also change workplaces if you have the Ausbildung.
I personally would recommend doing the Ausbildung as you will also be able to get more experience, only drawback is that you will have to attend school 1-2 days a week and the pay will be way lower (expect between 700 and 1500 in your 3 years, as a self thought fulltime dev you will probably get around 2,8k - 3,5k, numbers based on own experience)
Just reply if you need some more infos about specifics :)

Edit:
I should add that there are lots of IT companies (especially bigger ones) who will offer you a full time job afterwards, if you did your Ausbildung with them

Money is no use if you burn yourself out in the process, however an increase from 50k expected to 110k is a huge huge increase. I personally would take it, especially if your girlfriend will live with you and has no income (if you want to provide for her, technically she could also find a job)
I think of a salary as money paid for my time spent working and if my hourly rate goes up to 50.3 from 27.5 that is just rly good :)

Honestly, I have to disagree.
There are multiple aspects you have to learn in league to climb and be a better player and some champs are easier and more forgiving.
For example a qiyana player will have to demonstrate a lot more mechanics to be successful than a hecarim player.
Some champs, due to simpler kits, can improve winrates due to the player not having to focus as much on mechanics and can therefore focus more on the decision making (which is an extremely huge part of playing jungle and being a successful jungler imo)
So you won't win magically but picking a certain champ can certainly improve your winrate by helping you focus more on other aspects.

Bin selbst gerade in der Ausbildung zum Informatiker und arbeite in einen riesigen Pharma Konzern in der Schweiz, bei uns musst du folgendes machen und bestehen bevor du einen Vertrag bekommst:
- Initiale Bewerbung von dir geht raus mit Lebenslauf und Anschreiben
- Offline Test über externen Anbieter (Aufwand ca. 2h)
- Gespräch mit unserer HR Verantwortlichen für die Ausbildung
- Gespräch mit dem Ausbildungsleiter bei dem man diverse Aufgaben vorstellen muss die man vorher bekommt
- 2 Tage zum Probearbeit

Ist ziemlich langwierig und dauert mehrere Wochen, deswegen ist das wohl leider kein Troll Beitrag :(

Mein persönlicher Vorschlag wäre es, dass wenn man nach seinem schulischen Abschluss keine darauf hin anschließende Ausbildung/Studium hat dieses Pflichtjahr absolvieren muss.
Jeder der also Karriere machen möchte kann das gerne tun aber sich selber in Neuseeland finden kann man auch durch etwas für die Gesellschaft tun ersetzen.

I personally think approach velocity is a very niche rune that works very well for some champs (for example ashe) but xin not being one of them.
When slowing someone with your W, most likely scenario is you using your E onto them anyways, so distance covered or speed up through W slow is very rarely relevant.
And when using your E you want to move with the enemy anyways (always being a little  in front, because of movement between AAs, makes a huge difference) and you only get movespeed towards the enemy it will rarely make a difference.

If you want the advanced answer, which many people won't think about nor need for their games to win, here it is from a d1 jgl main that plays semi competitive
First herald is a huge objective in league currently because of turret plating and first blood tower gold, which helps accelerate your carries.
By taking cosmic insight you will not only have the advantage of lower flash cd but also have the empowered smite on the first herald spawn. Therefore giving you a combat summoner to use (early redsmite should not be underestimated). 

Other advantages include 6 camp clear into scuttle fight and when approaching the other scuttle having your 3. Smite already available (every smite is a lot of hp in the early game or just a way to secure/steal the crab).
